Method of Attack: Distributed via phishing emails or dropped by other malware
Uses compromised MikroTik routers as proxies for command and control servers
Uses default credentials, brute force attacks, and exploits CVE-2018-14847 to gain access to MikroTik routers
Creates NAT rules on routers to reroute traffic to remote C2 servers
Uses custom SSH commands on MikroTik devices
Acts as a malware botnet for resource-intensive operations such as DDoS attacks
Attack Vector: Exploitation of default credentials and brute force attacks on MikroTik routers
Exploitation of CVE-2018-14847 directory traversal vulnerability
Remote unauthenticated access to MikroTik devices
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of NAT rules redirecting port 449 to port 80 on remote C2 servers
Suspicious scheduled tasks, traffic redirection rules, DNS cache poisoning, default port changes, non-default users, suspicious files, proxy, socks, and firewall rules on MikroTik devices
Use of port 8291 (WinBox protocol) exposed externally
Use of default or weak passwords on MikroTik devices
